sections.heading: The futur simple
sections.body:
Besides *aller* + infinitive, French has a one-word future, the **futur simple**. For most verbs, add the endings to the **infinitive** (verbs in **-re** drop the final e):

The endings look like *avoir* in the present: **-ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont**. Every form has an **r** before the ending.

sections.heading: Irregular stems
sections.body: Common verbs have an irregular stem (the endings stay the same): *être → je serai*, *avoir → j'aurai*, *aller → j'irai*, *faire → je ferai*, *venir → je viendrai*, *pouvoir → je pourrai*, *vouloir → je voudrai*, *devoir → je devrai*, *voir → je verrai*, *savoir → je saurai*, *falloir → il faudra*, *pleuvoir → il pleuvra*.

sections.heading: When to use it
sections.body:
- predictions: *Demain, il fera beau.* *Tu verras, ce sera génial !* (You'll see, it'll be great!)
- promises: *Je t'appellerai ce soir.* (I'll call you tonight.)
- plans further away or more formal: *L'année prochaine, j'irai au Japon.*
- after *quand* talking about the future, French uses the future (English uses the present): *Quand je serai grand, je serai pilote.* (When I grow up…)

*Aller* + infinitive is more common in conversation for near, certain plans; the futur simple is more neutral and used for predictions and promises.

sections.heading: Pronunciation: the nasal vowels again
sections.body: Many future forms end in nasal vowels: **-ons** /ɔ̃/ and **-ont** /ɔ̃/ sound the same — *nous parlerons*, *ils parleront*. Compare also *ils seront* /sə.ʁɔ̃/ and *ils sont* /sɔ̃/. Keep the three nasals apart: *vingt* [ɛ̃], *vent* [ɑ̃], *vont* [ɔ̃] — and listen for them in *Ils viendront dans un an* [ɛ̃ … ɔ̃ … ɑ̃ … ɑ̃].

examples: Demain, il fera beau.
Tomorrow the weather will be nice.
Tu verras, ce sera génial !
You'll see, it'll be great!
Je t'appellerai ce soir, promis.
I'll call you tonight, I promise.
L'année prochaine, j'irai au Japon.
Next year I'll go to Japan.
Nous finirons le travail vendredi.
We'll finish the work on Friday.
Quand je serai grand, je serai pilote.
When I grow up, I'll be a pilot.
Vous pourrez venir samedi ?
Will you be able to come on Saturday?
Il faudra réserver une table.
We'll have to book a table.
Ils viendront dans un an.
They'll come in a year.
Un jour, j'aurai une maison au bord de la mer.
One day I'll have a house by the sea.
Elle prendra le train de huit heures.
She'll take the eight o'clock train.
On verra !
We'll see!
